scope: Adenosine A2A/A3 receptors, inflammation/immune signalling (NF-kB, cytokines, macrophages, lymphocytes, neutrophils, mast cells, microglia), TRPC1-mitochondrial targets and ELF safety side

targets.name: Adenosine A2A / A3 receptor up-regulation (Bmax, cAMP, anti-inflammatory signalling)
targets.driver_explanation: Within the Ferrara/IGEA work the receptor-density effect is dose-like in amplitude and exposure time: in human neutrophils 0.2 and 0.5 mT were insufficient, 1 mT gave a significant A2A increase and 1.5-3.5 mT was a plateau (secondary source: Varani 2017 review of Varani 2002/2003), and in rat cortex 1.5 mT needed about 4 h whereas 3 mT gave the same ~2-fold rise after 2 h (Varani 2012 abstract). Amplitude was varied at fixed 75 Hz and 1.3 ms pulse, so B and dB/dt (and E) co-vary and the studies cannot separate them; frequency, pulse width and waveform were never varied. Receptor involvement itself does not seem waveform-specific: an independent group using a PhysioStim-like waveform (3.85 kHz pulses, 10 T/s slew, 4 h/day) found that CRISPR loss of A2A/A3 blunted PEMF-driven osteoblast differentiation (Kar 2021), but receptor density was not measured there. The A2A/A3 up-regulation literature is essentially one consortium; one independent tendon-cell study did not reach significance (Colombini 2020).

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Amplitude, time and temperature varied at fixed 75 Hz / 1.3 ms; human neutrophils (abstract only; amplitude series via Varani 2017 review)
discriminating_evidence.finding: A2A Bmax 126+-10 -> 215+-15 fmol/mg after 1 h; effect intensity-, time- and temperature-dependent; Kd unchanged. Review: no effect at 0.2-0.5 mT, effect from 1 mT, plateau 1.5-3.5 mT, rise between 30 and 120 min, stable to 240 min.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Amplitude x exposure-time matrix (1.5 vs 3 mT; 2/4/6 h) in rat cortex and cortical neurons (abstract only)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Cortical A2A about doubled at both amplitudes, but 1.5 mT needed 4 h and 3 mT needed 2 h; effect transient in intact organ, constant in isolated membranes (1.9- and 2.2-fold after 2 h). A1 and A2A mRNA unchanged. Verifies the "doubling at 1.5-3 mT" statement (2.0-fold) and shows an amplitude-time trade-off.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Single amplitude (1.5 mT chondrocytes, 2.5 mT osteoblasts), single 24 h duration; probe-coil measurement of induced voltage (full text)
discriminating_evidence.finding: A2A and A3 mRNA/protein/Bmax about 2.1-2.3x, Kd, A1 and A2B unchanged; functional gain in cAMP responses and PGE2/IL-6/IL-8/NF-kB suppression. No amplitude or frequency comparison; but full methods allow dB/dt to be computed.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Independent group, different waveform (PhysioStim-like, 3.85 kHz, 10 T/s slew, 4 h/day for up to 16 days); CRISPR knock-out/knock-in of Adora2A and Adora3 in MC3T3-E1 (full text)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Adora3 disruption markedly blunted PEMF-induced alkaline phosphatase and several osteoblast genes; Adora2A disruption delayed it and blunted cFos/Pthr1; Adora3 knock-in restored the response. Shows A2A/A3 dependence for a waveform with ~5x the Ferrara dB/dt, but did not measure receptor density; no B value given.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Independent group, same nominal 1.5 mT / 75 Hz / 10% duty, 48 h, human tendon cells (full text)
discriminating_evidence.finding: A2A Bmax rose 28.7 -> 53.3 fmol/mg (84.4 -> 135.8 with IL-1b) but not significantly; ADORA2A mRNA fell with IL-1b + PEMF (feedback); PGE2 and IL-6 fell only slightly. Partial null or cell-type/duration dependence.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Independent Korean group, different device (Corefacial), UVB fibroblasts, abstract only
discriminating_evidence.finding: PEMF restored A2AAR/PKA/cAMP and reduced IL-1b/NF-kB/MMP; authors state the data are consistent with but do not prove A2AAR involvement. PEMF parameters not in the abstract.

thresholds.B_note: Highest amplitude with no significant effect (0.2 and 0.5 mT tested), per review text; peak vs average not specified
thresholds.note: Secondary source (review); primary methods of Varani 2002 not read (abstract only; PMC retrieval blocked). Frequency and pulse width are the Ferrara standard, not verified from the primary paper.

thresholds.endpoint: A2A receptor density in human neutrophils
thresholds.B_note: Reported amplitude per review; peak vs mean not specified
thresholds.exposure: 30-120 min (rise); elevated by 90 min, stable to 240 min
thresholds.note: dB/dt computed ONLY by linear scaling of the measured 2.04 T/s at 1.5 mT (same coil/waveform assumed): 1.0/1.5 x 2.04 = 1.36 T/s. Primary-paper dose-response data not read.

thresholds.B_note: Lower edge of the 1.5-3.5 mT plateau (upper edge 3.5 mT), per review text

thresholds.endpoint: A2A Bmax ~2-fold in intact rat cerebral cortex
thresholds.preparation: Rat cortex (intact tissue) and cortical neurons
thresholds.B_note: Amplitude as stated in abstract; peak vs mean not specified
thresholds.waveform: pulsed (Ferrara system; frequency/pulse width not stated in the abstract)
thresholds.exposure: 4 h (2.0-fold in intact cortex); 6 h 1.4- to 1.8-fold

thresholds.B_note: Amplitude as stated in abstract
thresholds.waveform: pulsed (Ferrara system; frequency/pulse width not stated in the abstract)
thresholds.note: Same ~2-fold ceiling reached in half the time at 2x the amplitude; effect declines with longer exposure in whole organ (1.6- to 1.9-fold at 4 h).

thresholds.endpoint: A2A and A3 Bmax ~2.1-2.3x, cAMP and PGE2/IL-6/IL-8 modulation
thresholds.B_note: 1.5 +- 0.1 mT, measured in air with a Hall probe (+-1% uniformity); peak
thresholds.E_geometry: Dish/flask-scale peak E at the edge: (r/2)*dB/dt with r = 0.043 m (flask 9.2 x 8.2 cm, Merighi 2024), field assumed normal to the monolayer; NOT cell-scale
thresholds.note: Operating point, not a determined optimum: only one amplitude/duration was tested. Computed dB/dt = V/(N*A) = 2.0e-3 V /(50 x pi x (2.5e-3 m)^2) = 2.04 T/s from the reported induced voltage 2.0+-0.5 mV in a 50-turn, 0.5 cm ID probe coil. 1.5 mT / 2.04 T/s implies an edge time ~0.74 ms.

thresholds.endpoint: A2A and A3 Bmax ~2.2-2.4x
thresholds.B_note: 2.5 +- 0.2 mT, Hall probe in air; peak
thresholds.note: dB/dt scaled linearly from the 1.5 mT measurement (2.5/1.5 x 2.04 = 3.4 T/s) because the induced voltage was reported for the 2.0 mV set-up only; the exact coil setting for the osteoblast voltage is not separately stated. Only one amplitude tested.

thresholds.endpoint: A2A Bmax and IL-1b-potentiated A2A (664-708 fmol/mg) with cAMP, PGE2, IL-6, IL-8 modulation
thresholds.preparation: Chondrocytes and osteoblasts +- IL-1b 1 ng/ml (48 h)
thresholds.note: PEMF plus IL-1b raised A2A Bmax to 664+-56 (chondrocytes) and 708+-62 (osteoblasts) fmol/mg: potentiation of the inflammatory-induced receptor expression.

thresholds.endpoint: A2A receptor density (not significant) and mRNA (down-regulated with IL-1b)
thresholds.B_note: Nominal; not independently confirmed by me
thresholds.note: Not a threshold: the only non-significant Bmax change at the nominal Ferrara dose. Possible duration (48 h, feedback down-regulation of ADORA2A mRNA) or tendon-cell dependence. The paper cites 8-12 h as dose-dependent exposures in tendon cells.

thresholds.endpoint: Neuroprotection / ROS reduction via A2A-linked pathways
thresholds.B_note: 1.5 +- 0.2 mT; peak
thresholds.exposure: 4-72 h; N9 microglia 24 h reduced ROS by 33-39%; 90 min preserved mitochondrial membrane potential
thresholds.note: Protection of SH-SY5Y viability appeared only 6 h after a 24 h exposure.

targets.window_summary: Receptor up-regulation: threshold ~1 mT (neutrophils; 0.2-0.5 mT ineffective), plateau 1.5-3.5 mT at 75 Hz / 1.3 ms; exposure must be at least 30-120 min in neutrophils and 2-4 h in rat cortex; common operating point 1.5-2.5 mT, 24 h. Computed dB/dt at 1.5 mT ~2.0 T/s (from a measured 2.0 mV probe voltage); dish-scale E ~0.04 V/m (computed). No frequency, pulse-width or dB/dt comparison exists.
targets.replication_status: Essentially a single consortium (Ferrara/Borea/Varani/Vincenzi/Gessi/Merighi with IGEA co-authors); independent support partial (Colombini 2020 not significant; Kar 2021 functional dependence only; Byun 2026 abstract-level). No independent null of Bmax found in PubMed searches.
targets.caveats: Varani 2002 and Yap 2019 primary methods could not be read (Europe PMC rate-limited). Neutrophil dose-response numbers are from a review. Rat cortex frequency/pulse width not in abstract. Peak vs mean B not specified in the abstracts. Computed dB/dt relies on one probe-coil voltage and an assumed uniform scaling; E is dish-scale only and orientation of the coil to the monolayer is ambiguous.

targets.name: NF-kB / TNF-a / IL-1b / IL-6 / PGE2 / COX-2 anti-inflammatory axis
targets.driver_explanation: Anti-inflammatory effects are reported over a very wide range: 4 uT at 5 Hz (Selvam), 1 mT at 50 Hz (Vianale), 1.5 mT at 75 Hz pulses (Ferrara) and ~4 mT square wave at 5-8 Hz (Ross), while the same readouts go the other way at 0.8-1 mT sine 50-60 Hz in macrophages (Kim 2017, Frahm 2006). The only within-study frequency comparison (Ross 2013, ~4 mT, 5-30 Hz) found effect at 5.1-7.8 Hz and none at 10.8 Hz and above at fixed amplitude, i.e. a frequency window that does not scale with dB/dt (dB/dt rises with f). No study varied B and dB/dt independently in these readouts. The best candidates for the discriminating variable are frequency/pulse pattern (Ross; Chen 2021) and amplitude windows (Wang 2017; Sukumar 2026), but each rests on single groups.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Frequency series 5.1-30 Hz at fixed ~4 mT, 50% duty square wave, 1 h, LPS-challenged RAW264.7 (full text)
discriminating_evidence.finding: 5.1 and 7.8 Hz: TNF-a about -37%; 5.1 Hz: NF-kB about -60%; 10.8, 15.6, 20.8, 23.4 and 30 Hz: no effect. Effect does not increase with dB/dt: window at lowest frequencies. Edge time not reported so dB/dt not computable.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: 5 Hz vs 13 Hz comparison in CHO mu-opioid cells (abstract only)
discriminating_evidence.finding: 5 Hz stimulated a cAMP reduction larger than morphine (+23%), 13 Hz behaved like control. Supports narrow low-frequency window; same group.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: In vivo adjuvant arthritis, 4 uT at 5 Hz, 90 min (abstract only)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Lymphocyte PMCA activity and intracellular Ca2+ restored and PGE2 reduced at microtesla amplitude; indicates effects far below the mT regime (dB/dt computed ~1.3e-4 T/s).

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: 1 mT, 50 Hz sine in HaCaT, 1 h and 72 h (abstract only)
discriminating_evidence.finding: NF-kB p65 nearly undetectable after 1 h; RANTES/MCP-1/MIP-1a/IL-8 down after 72 h; cell growth up at 48 h.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: 0.8 mT, 60 Hz in RAW264.7 (abstract only)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Opposite polarity: NO, TNF-a, IL-1b, IL-6 up, NF-kB nuclear translocation, NFAT2 and Ca2+ influx up; antioxidant treatment worsened it. Inverse effect at B similar to Vianale.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: 50 Hz, 1.0 mT; 0.05-1.0 mT for free radicals (abstract only)
discriminating_evidence.finding: IL-1b 12.3-fold at 24 h, phagocytosis 1.6-fold at 45 min; free-radical formation significant at all tested flux densities 0.05-1.0 mT (45 min).

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Human post-operative dosing comparison (abstract only)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Q4 (20 min per 4 h) and Q2 (15 min per 2 h) schedules worked, a 5 min per 20 min schedule did not: schedule matters, more frequent short exposures lost the effect. Device parameters not given in abstract.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: 75 Hz, 1.5 mT, 24 h, bovine synovial fibroblasts +- adenosine deaminase (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: EMF lowered TNF-a/LPS-stimulated PGE2 and COX-2; the EMF effect was lost when endogenous adenosine was removed with adenosine deaminase -> adenosine-dependent.

thresholds.B_note: Reported "about 40 G" = 4 mT; waveform amplitude (square wave), peak assumed
thresholds.schedule: single exposure, cells challenged with LPS (3 h pre-challenge)
thresholds.note: Edge time not reported, so dB/dt and E left null. 7.8 Hz also effective for TNF-a.

thresholds.endpoint: TNF-a / NF-kB suppression disappears
thresholds.note: No effect at 10.8, 15.6, 20.8, 23.4 or 30 Hz at the same amplitude (frequency window, not an amplitude window).

thresholds.B_note: 1 mT as stated; peak vs rms not stated
thresholds.note: Computed assuming 1 mT is sine peak: 2*pi*50*1e-3 = 0.314 T/s. Operating point; no amplitude comparison.

thresholds.note: dB/dt borrowed from the 1.5 mT measurement in Vincenzi 2013 (same group/coil design), not measured in this paper.

thresholds.endpoint: PGE2, IL-6, IL-8 down, IL-10 up
thresholds.note: Amplitude, frequency and duration not stated in the abstract; Ferrara system.

thresholds.endpoint: IL-1b in CSF (up to 10-fold lower at 6 h)
thresholds.note: B and frequency not given in the abstract.

thresholds.endpoint: Post-operative pain/narcotic benefit lost with 5 min per 20 min schedule

thresholds.schedule: VAS at 24 h 87% (failed) vs 74% of the 1 h value (effective)
thresholds.note: Schedule-dependence (too-frequent short exposure lost the effect); B and frequency not given in the abstract.

thresholds.endpoint: Pro-inflammatory activation: NO, TNF-a, IL-1b, IL-6, NF-kB nuclear translocation, NFAT2, Ca2+ influx
thresholds.B_note: 0.8 mT as stated; peak vs rms not stated
thresholds.note: Computed assuming sine peak: 2*pi*60*0.8e-3 = 0.302 T/s.

thresholds.endpoint: IL-1b release 12.3-fold (24 h), phagocytosis 1.6-fold (45 min), free radicals (0.05-1.0 mT, 45 min)
thresholds.B_note: 1.0 mT as stated; free radical rise also at 0.05 mT
thresholds.note: Computed assuming sine peak 1.0 mT. Apparently no genotoxicity (micronuclei unchanged at 12-48 h).

targets.window_summary: Anti-inflammatory window is frequency/pattern-specific rather than a clear B or dB/dt window: effective at 5-8 Hz (~4 mT square wave), 50 Hz sine (1 mT), 75 Hz pulses (1.5 mT) and 5 Hz at 4 uT, but pro-inflammatory with 50-60 Hz sine at 0.8-1 mT in macrophages. Computed sine dB/dt of the effective and adverse cases overlaps (0.3 T/s), so dB/dt alone does not separate them.
targets.replication_status: Mixed: several groups report suppression (Ross, Vianale, Ferrara, Selvam) with different devices, but each parameter set is single-lab; contradictory pro-inflammatory results from independent labs (Kim 2017, Frahm 2006).
targets.caveats: Most records abstract-only. Rohde 2015 (exudate IL-1b 5-fold higher in sham at 24 h; pain 2x at 5 h and 4x at 72 h) and Taylor 2015 do not give device parameters in the abstracts; device type not verified. Peak vs rms of ELF sine amplitudes not specified in several abstracts.

targets.name: Macrophage M1/M2 polarisation (including inverse, pro-inflammatory effects)
targets.driver_explanation: Chen 2021 compared 22 blinded fields at near-identical fundamental frequency (51.8 vs 52.3 Hz) and amplitude (6-282 uT at 6 mm) and found that the send/pause pulse-burst pattern flipped M1 vs M2 outcomes, which cannot be explained by B or by dB/dt computed from the fundamental alone. Amplitude windows are additionally suggested: Sukumar 2026 (pulse barrage, 0-3 mT) found maximal M1 activation at 3 mT after one 10-min exposure whereas earlier work at uT-1.5 mT was anti-inflammatory; Wang 2017 (15 Hz, 0.5-3 mT) found opposite effects on osteoclast-lineage RAW264.7 cells at 0.5 and 3 mT. Each is a single lab, and none separates B from dB/dt.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: 22 blinded fields (Somagen), B 6-282 uT, fundamental 3.3-90.6 Hz, 7 or 30 min, PBMC-derived macrophages (full text)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Field A (51.8 Hz) M1-like (pSTAT1 x2.9, CD86 x2.0, ROS x1.4); field B (52.3 Hz) M2-like (arginase x2.6); differ in send-pause burst pattern, not in fundamental or amplitude. Extending 7 to 30 min did not raise marker effects, but cytokine secretion did.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Amplitude series 0, 0.5-3 mT drive, 15 Hz pulse barrage, single 10 min, 24 h read-out; TRPC1 and aminoglycoside/SKF-96365/2-APB blockers (full text)
discriminating_evidence.finding: 3 mT (vs 0 and 2 mT) gave strongest M1 markers (iNOS, CD86 up; PPAR-gamma, arginase down) in RAW264.7 and BMDM and repolarised IL-4 M2 cells; blocked by TRPC1 inhibitors. In vivo 4T1 tumours: 3 mT, 30 min twice weekly, 3 of 4 mice tumour free at 2 weeks (n=4).

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Intensity series 0.5/1/2/3 mT at 15 Hz, 2 h/day for 7 days, RAW264.7 + RANKL (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: 0.5 mT inhibits osteoclast formation and resorption, 3 mT enhances resorption via apoptosis (BAX up): an explicit intensity window with opposite sign.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: In vivo synovitis mice (DMM, air pouch), 1.5 mT, 75 Hz, 10% duty (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Reduced IL-1b/TNF-a, fewer neutrophils, more macrophages; enhanced efferocytosis with p38 phosphorylation inhibited.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Co-culture human tendon cells (IL-1b primed) and macrophages, parameters from earlier work (abstract only)
discriminating_evidence.finding: PEMF favoured a pro-regenerative macrophage phenotype and anti-inflammatory mediators, possibly via FAK signalling.

thresholds.endpoint: M1-like activation (CD86 x2.0, pSTAT1 x2.9, ROS x1.4)
thresholds.B_note: Up to 282 uT as the maximum of the 22-field set at 6 mm; per-field amplitude for field A not separately recorded by me
thresholds.waveform: burst/pulse pattern with fundamental 51.8 Hz (not sinusoidal)
thresholds.note: Computed upper bound as a sine-equivalent: 2*pi*52*282e-6 = 0.092 T/s; the actual waveform is non-sinusoidal so true dB/dt can be higher. Field B at 52.3 Hz gave an M2-like profile.

thresholds.endpoint: Maximal M1 markers (iNOS, CD86), repolarisation of IL-4 M2 cells
thresholds.B_note: 3 mT drive amplitude; 2 mT and 0 mT comparators
thresholds.waveform: pulse barrage: 20 x 150 us on/off pulses repeated for 6 ms, ~50 us rise to maximum
thresholds.burst: 20 pulses per 6 ms barrage at 15 Hz
thresholds.schedule: read-out at 24 h; NF-kB biphasic at 0.5 and 4 h
thresholds.note: Reported "~17 T/s" for 0.5-3 mT drive amplitudes; but 3 mT/50 us = 60 T/s and 1.5 mT/50 us = 30 T/s (computed), so the reported value is inconsistent with the stated rise time; flagged. E not reported.

thresholds.endpoint: Anti-inflammatory vs pro-inflammatory crossover
thresholds.B_note: Paper states prior macrophage work in uT to 1.5 mT range was anti-inflammatory (narrative); not a measured crossover in one study
thresholds.note: Placeholder for the amplitude polarity inversion; not independently measured. 2 mT was weaker than 3 mT.

thresholds.endpoint: Osteoclast formation and resorption inhibition
thresholds.note: Waveform and edge time not given in the abstract.

thresholds.endpoint: Osteoclast apoptosis (BAX up), enhanced resorption at high amplitude
thresholds.note: Opposite sign from 0.5 mT; 1 and 2 mT not detailed in the abstract.

thresholds.endpoint: Efferocytosis up, IL-1b/TNF-a down, synovitis score down
thresholds.preparation: C57BL/6 mice DMM synovitis and air pouch
thresholds.note: dB/dt borrowed from the Ferrara 1.5 mT measurement; waveform shape per abstract only "pulse waveform".

targets.window_summary: Polarity depends on pulse pattern and amplitude: M2/anti-inflammatory with uT-1.5 mT and 5-75 Hz stimuli, M1 with a 3 mT, 15 Hz pulse barrage (reported ~17 T/s, computed 30-60 T/s) and with certain 52 Hz burst patterns at <=282 uT. Not a B or dB/dt window.
targets.replication_status: Single groups for each pattern (Chen/Somagen; Sukumar/NUS; Wang/China); contradictory polarity between labs is the norm.
targets.caveats: Inverse (pro-inflammatory) effects are context dependent (tumour/infection vs injury). The Sukumar 4T1 result has n=4. Phase 1 cancer-patient safety statement is from the paper, not independently verified.

targets.name: TRPC1-Ca2+-(calcineurin/NFAT, PCAF)-PGC-1a mitochondrial biogenesis (magnetic mitohormesis)
targets.driver_explanation: The response is brief and low-dose (single 10 min, 1-1.5 mT pulses at 15 Hz in Franco-Obregon group studies) and is blocked by TRPC1 knock-down or aminoglycosides. Evidence against a purely induction-driven mechanism comes from the same group: downward-directed fields outperform upward-directed ones (Wong 2022), and the response is lost with growth in the dark, magnetic shielding or upward fields (Iversen 2025, CRY2-TRPC1 axis). Both point to a vector/orientation and light-linked (radical-pair-type) component. The authors also say pulses are chosen for clinically tolerable repeated delivery; the rationale for pulses is stated as "unclear" in the harmonisation review, with rise time, symmetry and direction seldom reported. The device reports are internally inconsistent about 1 vs 1.5 mT. B vs dB/dt was never separated by varying frequency at fixed B.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Single 10 min exposure, 1.5 mT amplitude; CRISPR TRPC1 knock-down, TRPM7 siRNA, aminoglycoside block, ambient-field deprivation (abstract only)
discriminating_evidence.finding: TRPC1-mediated Ca2+ entry, NFAT, PCAF and PGC-1a up; mitochondrial respiration up; TRPC1 knock-down abolished it, TRPM7 siRNA did not; removing ambient field lowered TRPC1 expression.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Directionally specific field (downward vs upward), 1.5 mT, 10 min (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Downward-directed field produced a greater secretome/EV response and TRPC upregulation than upward-directed; streptomycin blocked; direct exposure caused mild oxidative stress.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Dark growth, magnetic shielding, field direction and CRY2 (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Sensitivity depends on light and CRY2, and is lost with shielding or upward-directed field: vector and radical-pair-type involvement, not dB/dt alone.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Cell-derived vesicles with and without TRPC1 knock-down (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Vesicles carrying TRPC1 respond to PEMF with TRPC1-mediated Ca2+ entry; knock-down vesicles do not and can transfer responsiveness to recipient cells.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Concurrent optical and magnetic stimulation (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Magnetic plus light: supra-additive proliferation, lower ROS, higher ATP; aminoglycosides block.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Randomised pilot ACLR (n=10 vs 10), 1 mT peak, 10 min weekly for 16 weeks (full text)
discriminating_evidence.finding: 31P-MRS Pi/PCr, (Pi+PCr)/ATP, PDE/ATP improved and ceramides fell; discussion acknowledges magnetically induced oxidative stress could be harmful in inflamed, surgically injured tissue and a small developmental depression under direct exposure.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Narrative review of efficacy windows (full text)
discriminating_evidence.finding: States that low oxidative stress (lower amplitude, frequency or duration) gives the beneficial response and higher doses the opposite; 1.5 mT/10 min for myogenesis vs 3 mT/60 min for cancer-cell killing; potency lower if exposure is applied after log-phase expansion.

thresholds.endpoint: TRPC1-Ca2+-PGC-1a activation, mitochondriogenesis, respiration
thresholds.B_note: Amplitude stated as 1.5 mT; the device is described elsewhere as "1 mT @ 15 Hz", so amplitude is uncertain
thresholds.waveform: pulse barrage per Sukumar 2026 device description: 20 x 150 us on/off pulses repeated for 6 ms, ~50 us rise
thresholds.note: Computed 1.5 mT/50 us = 30 T/s only if the device waveform is the one described in Sukumar 2026 (assumption, not shown for Yap 2019). Full text not read.

thresholds.endpoint: Myogenesis / mitochondria / PGC-1a
thresholds.B_note: 1.5 mT as stated
thresholds.note: Pgc-1a up after 2 months alone; oxidative muscle and fatty-acid oxidation after >4 months. Exercise alone did not raise Pgc-1a in 6 weeks.

thresholds.endpoint: Human mitochondrial energetics (31P-MRS), ceramides
thresholds.B_note: 1 mT peak
thresholds.note: n=10 per arm; no dB/dt reported.

thresholds.endpoint: Myogenic potency reduced / oxidative stress emerges
thresholds.note: Review states that higher amplitude, frequency or duration shifts the response toward oxidative stress; and that 3 mT/60 min kills cancer cells. No numeric dose-response within one study; potency is lost when exposure is applied after log-phase expansion.

thresholds.endpoint: Mild oxidative stress with direct exposure
thresholds.note: Directly exposed cells show mild oxidative stress while conditioned medium does not.

thresholds.endpoint: Metabolic benefit in humans
thresholds.exposure: 10 min per visit, alternate legs, 12 weekly sessions
thresholds.note: No overall HbA1c/glucose/HOMA-IR change; subgroup with central obesity improved (HbA1c 7.5 -> 7.1%). B not given in the abstract. Well tolerated, no adverse events.

targets.window_summary: Brief (10 min) exposures at ~1-1.5 mT, 15 Hz pulses, weekly; direction-, light- and TRPC1-dependent. More exposure (3 mT/60 min) or later-phase exposure reverses the benefit in the same literature (review-level). Computed dB/dt of the device is 30-60 T/s if the 50 us rise applies; not independently verified.
targets.replication_status: Single group (Franco-Obregon, NUS; Iversen/Yap/Sukumar/Wong), with external TRPC/CRY-related biophysics unproven; small human pilots; the T2DM study was mostly null overall.
targets.caveats: Yap 2019 full text not read (blocked); the 1.0 vs 1.5 mT inconsistency; rise time is borrowed from Sukumar 2026. Stephenson 2022 is a pilot with n=10 per arm.

targets.name: Mitochondrial function, ROS and antioxidant (MnSOD) adaptation: other labs
targets.driver_explanation: Independent labs report adaptive antioxidant (MnSOD) induction and reduced ROS after repeated short PEMF exposures (Osera 2015, Falone 2016), reduced ROS with maintained mitochondrial membrane potential (Merighi 2024) and dose-dependent mitochondrial effects with exposure time (Ivanov 2026). A 30 kHz sine-burst device showed ATP-synthesis-linked respiration stimulation but failed to rescue NO-inhibited respiration (Zavadskis 2026). Another group found a shift from mitochondrial respiration to glycolysis at 4 mT and 80 Hz (Liao 2025). There is no B vs dB/dt discrimination; the data are of the exposure-time (dose) type.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Exposure time series, 1 vs 5 min/h for 10 nights, broadband pulsed device (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Antioxidant potential +8% (n.s.) at minimum exposure vs +20.6% at maximum; thymocyte mitochondrial fluorescence +29% at the maximum only: dose-dependent.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Cultures, homogenates and isolated mitochondria; 1 ms, 30 kHz sine burst (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: ATP-synthesis-linked respiration selectively stimulated; no rescue of NO-inhibited respiration; blue light did rescue.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: L929 fibroblasts, 4 mT, 80 Hz (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Migration/viability up, shift to glycolysis, low ROS; vesicular transport up.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: 2 mT, 75 Hz, 15 min x 3 over 5 days, SK-N-BE(2) (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: MnSOD-based protection up and ROS down after H2O2 challenge.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: 10 min x 4 per week (40 min total), SH-SY5Y (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: MnSOD activity up and ROS down after 30 min H2O2; B not stated in the abstract.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: 10 uT oscillating field at 12-33 Hz on a 45 uT static field, HT-1080 cells (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Proliferation accelerated or inhibited depending on frequency near 16.5 Hz and a 0.5 Hz or 250 nT shift: radical-pair-type sensitivity; weak-field regime.

targets.replication_status: Independent labs exist (Osera/Falone, Liao, Zavadskis, Ivanov) but with non-matching parameters; no direct replication. Searches for Calabro, Gualdi and Kuhn mitochondrial PEMF papers returned no PubMed hits and were not included.
targets.caveats: All abstract-only. Zavadskis 2026 and Ivanov 2026 are recent single reports.

targets.name: Immune-cell Ca2+ signalling (lymphocytes/Jurkat, thymocytes; calcineurin/NFAT)
targets.driver_explanation: Liburdy 1992 is the cleanest B vs E discrimination in this scope: using a multi-ring annular culture plate based on Faraday induction, thymocyte Ca2+ influx (plateau phase of mitogen signalling) depended on the induced E at constant B, and a pure 60 Hz E-field matched a magnetically induced E-field of the same strength. Independent replication of 50 Hz Jurkat Ca2+ oscillations (Lindstrom 1993 at 0.1 mT) is mixed: Mattsson 2001 found a weaker response in Jurkat cells from three sources, and a blinded multi-laboratory repeat at 0.15 mT (Wey 2000) found no difference between field, sham and no-field. McCreary 2002 found effects only after correcting for cell-cycle and anti-CD3 covariates. A 4.75 T static + 0.7 mT pulsed NMR exposure raised Ca2+ in normal lymphocytes and lowered it in Jurkat cells without pro-inflammatory output (Aldinucci 2003).

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Multi-ring annular culture plate: E varied at constant B; pure E-field vs magnetically induced E (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Ca2+ influx increased in the plateau phase of mitogen signalling at 22 mT, 60 Hz, E = 1.7 mV/cm; scaled with induced E; pure E matched; Ca2+ channel implicated.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: 50 Hz, 0.1 mT sinusoidal, single-cell fura-2 imaging, Jurkat (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Acute Ca2+ oscillations that stopped when the field was off; comparable to anti-CD3 effect.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Blinded RAPID programme repeat, 1.5 G (0.15 mT) 50 Hz, 8 min; MF vs sham vs no field (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Transient incidence 16.5 / 14.6 / 14.2% (MF / sham / no field), no significant difference: null replication of Lindstrom.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Replication with 50 Hz, 0.15 mT in Jurkat E6-1 cells from three sources (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Responses were seen but at lower percentage than the original.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: 60 Hz 100 uT peak, 78 uT static, combined; covariate analysis (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Effects only appeared after cell-cycle and anti-CD3 correction.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: 4.75 T static + 0.7 mT pulsed NMR, 1 h, human lymphocytes and Jurkat (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Ca2+ up in normal lymphocytes, down in Jurkat; no pro-inflammatory cytokines.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Model paper: activation-dependent and biphasic responses (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Proposes that effects depend on cell activation state and may be biphasic, explaining irreproducibility.

targets.window_summary: Effects reported from 0.1 mT at 50-60 Hz (computed dB/dt 0.03-0.05 T/s) up to 22 mT (reported E 0.17 V/m); independent replications at 0.1-0.15 mT were null or weak. The E-metric experiment is the only one that tests the driver directly.
targets.replication_status: Contested: single-lab positives (Lindstrom, Liburdy) with weak or null independent replications (Wey blinded repeat, Mattsson, McCreary).
targets.caveats: Abstract-only; Liburdy dose in B (22 mT) is high relative to therapeutic or environmental 50 Hz exposures; E magnitude 0.17 V/m is the reported value.

targets.name: Innate immune cells: neutrophil ROS, mast-cell degranulation, microglia
targets.driver_explanation: Neutrophil superoxide inhibition is tied to A2A density and shows intensity, time and temperature dependence (Varani 2002), while ELF fields at 0.1 mT enhanced the PMA burst by 12.4% in rat neutrophils (Roy 1995), so polarity depends on the stimulus and the field. Mast cells showed no response at 5 mT, 60 Hz for 0.5-2 h (Price 1998, null). Microglia (N9) show reduced TNF-a/IL-1b via JNK (Merighi 2020) and reduced ROS (Merighi 2024) with the Ferrara 1.5 mT, 75 Hz protocol. No design separated B from dB/dt.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Neutrophils (abstract only)
discriminating_evidence.finding: Receptor density and agonist potency increased; superoxide inhibition by A2A agonists enhanced; intensity-, time- and temperature-dependent.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: 0.1 mT, 60 Hz, primed rat peritoneal neutrophils, PMA, DCFH real time (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: PMA-induced burst fluorescence +12.4% under field (n=5, P<0.02).

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: 5 mT, 60 Hz solenoid, rat peritoneal mast cells, 30 min to 2 h, 37 C (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: No degranulation and no change in 48/80 sensitivity: null.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: N9 microglia (existing library)
discriminating_evidence.finding: TNF-a and IL-1b reduced via a JNK-dependent pathway.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: N9 microglia, SH-SY5Y; time series 4-72 h (full text)
discriminating_evidence.finding: ROS reduced 33-39% after 24 h in N9; 90 min preserved membrane potential.

thresholds.B_note: 0.1 mT as stated
thresholds.note: Computed 2*pi*60*0.1e-3 = 0.0377 T/s (assuming peak). Direction is pro-oxidant.

targets.window_summary: Ferrara protocol (1.5 mT, 75 Hz, 1.3 ms) reduces ROS/cytokines in neutrophils and microglia; 60 Hz sine fields at 0.1 mT increase neutrophil burst, and 5 mT does not affect mast cells.
targets.replication_status: Single group for the protective effects; ELF pro-oxidant and null results from separate labs.

targets.name: Safety side: ICNIRP/IARC limits and the 0.3-0.4 uT childhood-leukaemia association
targets.driver_explanation: ICNIRP 2010 limits are expressed as induced E in the CNS (basic restriction) and B (reference level), i.e. they are induction-based. The childhood-leukaemia association is for 24 h average residential magnetic field categories of 0.3-0.4 uT and above (about three orders of magnitude below therapeutic mT levels); it is an epidemiological association, not shown to be causal, and the mechanism (B, dB/dt, E, contact currents, or confounding) is unknown. IARC 2002 classified ELF magnetic fields as possibly carcinogenic (2B) on this basis.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Pooled analysis of 9 studies (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: For <0.4 uT (99.2% of children) estimates were near the null; for >=0.4 uT (44 cases, 62 controls) RR 2.00 (1.27-3.13); selection bias may explain part.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Pooled analysis of 12 studies (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: >0.3 uT vs 0-0.1 uT OR 1.7 (1.2-2.3); 0.1-0.2 and 0.2-0.3 uT showed little or no association; US population-attributable fraction 3% (-2% to 8%).

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Seven post-2000 studies, 10,865 cases (abstract)
Power-line proximity pooled analysis (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: OR 1.33 (0.92-1.93) for <50 m from 200+ kV lines; no association with calculated magnetic field.

discriminating_evidence.design_feature: Pooled analysis of four recent studies (abstract)
discriminating_evidence.finding: OR 1.01 for >=0.4 uT vs <0.1 uT; the meta-analysis of the three pooled analyses gave 1.45 (0.95-2.20).

thresholds.endpoint: Childhood leukaemia (association, 24 h average residential field)
thresholds.B_note: 0.4 uT category cut-point of the 24 h average residential field (time-weighted mean, NOT a peak; if sinusoidal the peak would be ~1.41x an rms value)
thresholds.E_geometry: (r/2)*dB/dt with r = 0.1 m (rough head/torso scale, assumed)
thresholds.note: Computed 2*pi*50*0.4e-6 = 1.26e-4 T/s assuming 0.4 uT is sine amplitude. Association only; RR 2.00 (1.27-3.13) for >=0.4 uT (44 cases, 62 controls). 99.2% of children were below 0.4 uT.

thresholds.endpoint: Childhood leukaemia (association)
thresholds.B_note: 0.3 uT category cut-point (time-weighted mean field)
thresholds.note: Computed 2*pi*50*0.3e-6 = 9.4e-5 T/s. OR 1.7 (1.2-2.3) vs 0-0.1 uT; no clear association below 0.3 uT.

thresholds.endpoint: Childhood leukaemia (association)
thresholds.B_note: >=0.3 uT category
thresholds.note: OR 1.44 (0.88-2.36); weaker in recent studies, imprecise.

thresholds.endpoint: ICNIRP 2010 general-public reference level for B
thresholds.B_note: 200 uT rms at 50 Hz = 0.283 mT peak (converted); occupational 1000 uT rms. Values from a garbled PDF extraction: to be re-verified against the original
thresholds.note: Computed from the peak: 2*pi*50*0.283e-3 = 0.0889 T/s. At 10 Hz the public reference is 500 uT rms. Pulsed therapy at 1.5 mT peak and 75 Hz is numerically ~5x the public peak value but pulse shape and duty cycle must be assessed with the induced-E restriction, not B alone.

thresholds.endpoint: ICNIRP 2010 CNS basic restriction (induced E, rms)
thresholds.E_geometry: General public 0.02 V/m rms at 50 Hz; occupational 0.1 V/m; 10-25 Hz public 0.01 V/m, occupational 0.05 V/m (from a garbled PDF extraction; verify)
thresholds.note: Computed dish-scale E for the Ferrara 1.5 mT pulses (~0.044 V/m) is the same order as this restriction; the cell dish is not tissue and the comparison is only a magnitude check.

thresholds.endpoint: IARC 2002 classification
thresholds.note: ELF magnetic fields classed as 2B (possibly carcinogenic) based on the childhood-leukaemia association (stated in Zaryabova 2013 abstract; the IARC monograph abstract itself was not available). WHO EHC 238 (2007) and NTP 1998 were not retrievable from PubMed and are not verified.

targets.window_summary: Epidemiological association appears at 24 h mean residential fields of about 0.3-0.4 uT and above (OR 1.4-2.0, imprecise, weaker in recent studies); ICNIRP public reference 200 uT rms at 50 Hz and CNS induced-E restriction 0.02 V/m rms. Therapeutic pulsed mT fields are 3-4 orders of magnitude above the epidemiological category field.
targets.replication_status: Pooled analyses consistently show elevated but imprecise ORs at >=0.3-0.4 uT; recent pooled data show attenuation (OR 1.01 for >=0.4 uT in four recent studies); causality is not established.
targets.caveats: Association, not causation; selection bias and confounding (e.g. traffic, wire code) are discussed in the primary papers. A typical residential 50/60 Hz field magnitude is not quoted from a verified abstract here (Ahlbom reports 99.2% of children below 0.4 uT); ICNIRP numbers need re-verification. The IARC monograph abstract was not accessible.

new_refs.authors_short: Varani K, Vincenzi F, Ravani A, et al.
new_refs.title: Adenosine Receptors as a Biological Pathway for the Anti-Inflammatory and Beneficial Effects of Low Frequency Low Energy Pulsed Electromagnetic Fields.

cross_cutting_notes: Dose variable by group: Ferrara/IGEA uses 1.3 ms pulses at 75 Hz (computed ~2 T/s at 1.5 mT from a measured 2.0 mV probe voltage; dish-scale E ~0.04 V/m); Ross uses 5-30 Hz square waves at ~4 mT; Franco-Obregon/NUS uses 15 Hz pulse barrages (rise ~50 us; reported ~17 T/s inconsistent with 3 mT/50 us = 60 T/s); Kar 2021 used 3.85 kHz pulses at 10 T/s slew. A2A/A3 involvement appears across these very different dB/dt values (2 to 60 T/s), which argues against dB/dt as the sole trigger, but B and dB/dt were never decoupled. The only direct E-vs-B experiment in scope is Liburdy 1992 (thymocyte Ca2+, E reported 0.17 V/m at 22 mT, 60 Hz). Mast-cell and Jurkat Ca2+ nulls were found; independent nulls of A2A Bmax were not found. Not found in PubMed with simple searches: Calabro, Gualdi, Kuhn mitochondrial PEMF papers. Methods of Varani 2002 and Yap 2019 were not read (Europe PMC HTTP 429); Byun 2026 has a PMC full text (PMC13566763) that was not read. Epidemiology is reported strictly as association; a typical residential field value is not supplied because no verified abstract states one. Sub-note: the Sukumar 2026 statement that prior macrophage work at uT-1.5 mT was anti-inflammatory is a narrative statement, not a measured crossover. Li 2019 (high-voltage E-field pulses) and Piredda 2026 (>2 T multifrequency pulses) were screened out as not therapeutic magnetic-field studies.
